newsitem.title: USA: US crudes accumulate strength in outrights, grades.
newsitem.headline: US crudes accumulate strength in outrights, grades.

text.p: Outright cash and U.S. domestic crude grades gained Tuesday on bullish technical and fundamental factors, lifting prompt benchmark crude above the $20.00 a barrel level late in the session.
August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing stood around 30-35 cents higher at $20.10-20 a barrel, pulling the front month even to September WTI/Cushing.
Markets advanced on the NYMEX from the opening bell, accumulating technical strength as the session progressed.

Cash grades continued to build bullish momentum heading into the long Independence Day weekend in the U.S. Both sweet and sour barrels saw premiums gain and discounts trimmed against the surging benchmark.
Firm North Sea Brent values aided the grades, notably LLS sweet parcels, trade sources said.
"The grades rolled along with the lack of foreign avails," said a crude trader in Texas.

Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sold between a 20-25 cents premium, gaining around 7-8 cents from Monday. Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire moved around a 20 cents discount, 10 cents firmer than yesterday, while Midland/WTI steadied at 30 cents under August WTI/Cushing.
Sour barrels sold between $1.00-10 under August WTI/Cushing, again, some 10-15 cents stronger than Monday.

Inventory statistics released late Tuesday by the American Petroleum Insitute (API) showed crude stocks 4.36 million barrels lower, gasoline stocks down 1.23 million barrels and distillates gaining 4.02 million barrels.
Refinery utilization rates slipped to 96.9 percent from 97.6 percent, according to the API data.
